Reviewed current semantic head `7aa3c1910075a02287b0815867026a500187594f`. The prior retry-after-base-path-change correction is present. One additional P2 finding remains: a shortened worktree name is treated as a directive identity without a full ownership binding. The inline finding supplies two actual colliding IDs and the source path to reuse.

### Evidence and limits

- Independently recomputed the SHA-256 tags and shortened directory names for the two distinct IDs. Traced the current PowerShell source from lookup through repository registration and invocation. **No Windows worker tick was executed in this review.**

- Seven exact-head workflow runs succeeded. Draft/non-implementation gate steps and the actual HawkScan scan were skipped. Those badges are not admission or dynamic-security proof.

### Scope and next acceptance

Persistent pre-wake/fetch failures and cross-checkout coordination already belong to stacked [PR #175](https://github.com/SaCH-PRO/KEYFLOWOS/pull/175); they are not duplicate new findings against #169. Revalidate the corrected head against current main, then review #175's dependent revision.

This is a GitHub **COMMENT** review carrying a substantive CHANGES_REQUIRED result because the connected account owns the PR. It is not a typed #80 authority event, worker reassignment, admission, merge grant or installed-worker result. F9 remains the current assignment. PR stays draft/unmerged; application credit remains zero.

inline_comments.body:
**[P2] Verify full directive ownership before reusing a shortened worktree**

The 8-hex tag is only the first four SHA-256 bytes. These two distinct valid IDs both produce `86c85112`:

```text
CG-DIRECTIVE-LONG-PACKET-NAME-LONG-PACKET-NAME-INTEGRATION-CORRECTION-081631
CG-DIRECTIVE-LONG-PACKET-NAME-LONG-PACKET-NAME-INTEGRATION-CORRECTION-095457
```

Both have length 76 and share their first 70 characters. With room 32, both directory names are `CG-DIRECTIVE-LONG-PACKE-86c85112`. More generally, every shortened prefix of these IDs satisfies the current prefix check.

If the first directive leaves a retained worktree, this function accepts it as the second directive's sole match. `New-WakeWorktree` at lines 545–559 then bypasses base resolution and reuses it; `Test-RegisteredWorktree` only verifies membership in this repository, not ownership by the complete directive ID. `Invoke-ClaudeForDirective` changes into that directory before waking Claude. Failed attempts and dirty successful attempts can retain partial work, so the later task can execute in the earlier task's tree.

Bind ownership to the complete raw directive ID or full digest before reuse. A conflicting ID must receive a distinct owned worktree or a counted refusal. Use this pair as a deterministic retained-partial-work regression, preserving same-ID retry reuse after base path changes and ambiguous-match rejection.

The collision computation was executed locally; the routing consequence follows from the exact source. A Windows worker-tick reproduction was not run here.
inline_comments.author: SaCH-PRO

inline_comments.body:
**[P2] Refuse stale-lock reclamation unless the coordinating mutex was acquired**

`WaitOne(30000)` may return false, and the outer catch may also leave `$owned` false. Both paths still enter the read/remove/create loop. The atomic `CreateNew` operation does not protect the preceding stale-read/delete transaction.

Two starters from different checkouts can both read the same stale machine-lock owner. A deletes that stale file, creates its own fresh lock and returns success. B then executes its already-decided unconditional `Remove-Item`, deleting A's fresh lock, and creates its own. Both workers have returned success from acquisition. The file stream is closed before `New-LockFile` returns, so it does not prevent B's later removal.

Require successful mutex ownership before this transaction, or use another mechanism that serializes the complete reclaim operation. On mutex construction/acquisition failure or timeout, fail closed without deleting a lock or waking Claude. Add targeted failure/timeout proof and live negative controls while retaining the existing successful concurrent-start and stale-owner tests.

This is a source-control-flow finding with a concrete interleaving, not a locally observed Windows race. The current four-starter test covers the normal mutex path and does not exercise either failure branch.
inline_comments.author: SaCH-PRO
